title: Which people, claims and records the OCC's stablecoin rule covers
description: Complete saved reading and source links
search_context: Research Packages/Fintech and Private Rails/Retail Payment Terminal Transition 2026-07-28/genius-implementation-gap-2026-08-17/OCC Full Rule Reading 2026-10-21/WAVE 01 SCOPE DEFINITIONS.md What this wave adds 1. A customer and a holder are different people in law 2. Reserve obligations follow redemption liability, not raw mint counts 3. Issuer-level and consolidated measurements are deliberately different 4. A wrapper redeemable for another stablecoin generally falls outside this payment-stablecoin definition 5. Payment need not be the token's primary purpose 6. The issuer is the obligor; the vendor is not automatically an issuer 7. Custody eligibility is not deposit eligibility 8. Some credit unions become nonbanks for this particular rule 9. The OCC reserves a separate decision about some forms of “money” 10. A significant U.S.-customer footnote reaches beyond physical location 11. Territories can appear in both geographic definitions without every territory issuer being foreign 12. A private key need not exist as a complete stored string 13. Public wallet data and private identity-linking data are treated differently 14. Read the ledger footnote before calling every private database a distributed ledger 15. The rule treats formal titles as less important than actual governance functions 16. A new general reservation of authority is distinct from transition waivers 17. Statutory provisions can matter even where no new CFR text appears 18. The opening footnotes reveal affirmative refusals and unfinished legal work Corrections and additions to the first overview Connections to the existing library Next wave and unresolved tests

title: What issuers may do, and who decides whether rewards break the law
description: Complete saved reading and source links
search_context: Research Packages/Fintech and Private Rails/Retail Payment Terminal Transition 2026-07-28/genius-implementation-gap-2026-08-17/OCC Full Rule Reading 2026-10-21/WAVE 02 ACTIVITIES REWARDS AND BRANDS.md Answer and reading scope 1. Four distinct questions replace a single approved/not-approved label 2. Direct support is broader than strict necessity, but not an unlimited business charter 3. Activity clarification is discretionary, with no promised response clock 4. An issuer can transact in payment stablecoins it did not issue 5. Native-token holdings are permitted for fees/testing, with an excess-disposal expectation 6. Non-dollar coins can be permitted; their backing can create FX risk 7. Collateral trusts are allowed with conditions, but not assumed to remove reserves from the issuer's balance sheet 8. Issuer deposits can still fund bank investment; fiduciary reserve property is different 9. Standard custody liens and clearing liens survive within bounded exceptions 10. Repo is a permitted liquidity tool, with purpose limits but no tracing of each borrowed dollar 11. The rule's repo preapproval is real but narrower than several requests 12. Marketing may identify a permitted issuer, but may not imply an approved government coin 13. Rewards: substance matters even after the presumption is removed 14. The deposit-flight debate remains an empirical dispute in this source 15. Good-faith reliance is relevant, not a complete anti-evasion safe harbor 16. National trust-bank powers survive, but all applicable restrictions still apply 17. Multi-brand protection depends on actual legal arrangements, not branding 18. OCC expressly declines additional white-label transparency requirements 19. Coordination does not mean identical agency rules 20. A global coin is not a single global permission or group-wide reserve promise What the second wave changes in our understanding Follow-through

title: Custody protects particular claims, while approval attaches to the issuer
description: Complete saved reading and source links
search_context: Research Packages/Fintech and Private Rails/Retail Payment Terminal Transition 2026-07-28/genius-implementation-gap-2026-08-17/OCC Full Rule Reading 2026-10-21/WAVE 06 CUSTODY AND DOMESTIC APPLICATIONS.md Answer and evidence boundary 1. The custody perimeter is narrower than all stablecoin wallets 2. Customer property requires contracts and records, not merely an address balance 3. Neither proof technology nor a custody label decides the legal relationship 4. Control is a necessary-consent test, not unilateral transfer power 5. Sub-custody delegates holding, while retaining oversight duties 6. The rule does not establish a universal custody-release deadline 7. Custody priority can be expressly subordinated; issuer insolvency is a different rule 8. Lawful custody charges can reduce assets; aggregate backing remains the issuer's duty 9. A deposit is permitted custody cash treatment, but remains a bank credit relationship 10. Omnibus permission depends on whose assets are mixed, and where 11. Gas-fee convenience does not create another commingling exception 12. The hardware/software exclusion also tests representations and the source of legal authority 13. Custody reporting and key valuation do not supply a complete operational-risk map 14. Bridges receive a fact-specific legal analysis, not categorical clearance 15. Publication of decisions is not the requested authorization registry 16. Prefiling is optional; an MSB registration does not prove AML compliance 17. Intake, completeness and the decision period use separate clocks 18. The issuer application is comprehensive for its activity, but does not grant a bank charter 19. Review reaches individuals, corporate owners and the nonfinancial-public-company gate 20. Conditional approval is permission with conditions, not the first half of a routine two-stage issuer license 21. The new safety factor is broad; the whole commenter checklist was not codified 22. Public comment is discretionary; adverse decisions have specified review routes 23. Transition waiver can reach issuance itself, but a pending filing is not relief 24. The application notice adds business-model flexibility, not group-wide licensing Corrections and qualifications to the initial overview Connections to the earlier Library Next work

title: What counts as stablecoin backing, and when the reserves fail
description: Complete saved reading and source links
search_context: Research Packages/Fintech and Private Rails/Retail Payment Terminal Transition 2026-07-28/genius-implementation-gap-2026-08-17/OCC Full Rule Reading 2026-10-21/WAVE 03 RESERVES LIQUIDITY AND CUSTODY.md Answer and scope 1. Continuous fair-value backing survives the comments without an intraday grace exception 2. Identifiable reserves do not become a mandatory token-to-asset public tracing system 3. Excess can be withdrawn more often, but today's excess may still be needed as a buffer 4. A repo agreement on paper may not demonstrate usable liquidity 5. No universal 1% buffer, but more than 100% backing can be necessary 6. Asset eligibility has several different maturity and structure tests 7. A qualifying ETF can be a reserve; a generic Treasury fund may not qualify 8. Tokenization earns neither a universal haircut nor a universal presumption of liquidity 9. The final rule's numerical floors and caps are not the proposal's full safe harbor 10. A Reserve Bank is not exempt from the counterparty cap 11. Some custody exposures are exempt, but the issuer must earn the exemption through conduct 12. Worked counterparty examples illustrate the different legal exposures 13. Self-custody and affiliate custody remain possible, without a universal fiduciary mandate 14. The issuer retains reserve-sufficiency responsibility; the bank/custodian need not verify the aggregate by default 15. Deposits must be withdrawable in substance; placement networks are allowed conditionally 16. Public report, accountant examination and officer certification have different visibility and clocks 17. OCC declines universal surprise attestations but preserves supervisory access 18. One brand on multiple chains can use one reserve pool 19. Three different problems have different consequences 20. Fifteen consecutive business days is a liquidation trigger, not a lawful shortfall period 21. Secondary-market price is a supervisory signal, not the backing denominator Corrections and refinements to the first overview Next wave

title: Who can redeem, what starts the clock, and which controls must work
description: Complete saved reading and source links
search_context: Research Packages/Fintech and Private Rails/Retail Payment Terminal Transition 2026-07-28/genius-implementation-gap-2026-08-17/OCC Full Rule Reading 2026-10-21/WAVE 04 REDEMPTION AND OPERATIONAL RISK.md Answer and scope 1. A wholesale business model cannot eliminate the obligation to redeem from other holders 2. A redemption request itself makes a holder a customer for this purpose 3. The clock has a conditional start and a carefully defined endpoint 4. The ceiling does not confer cash-equivalent or margin-collateral status 5. Stress notice, extension requests and an actual extension are separate events 6. Foreign licensing and other law can prevent a redemption without violating this requirement 7. The civil-order proposal is not a uniform new queue-priority rule 8. Redemption fees can affect net proceeds, including for small or foreign requests 9. Disclosures reach holders, while some direct notice duties reach current customers 10. No standardized template, identifier requirement or blanket irreversibility warning is added 11. Risk rules borrow bank-control practices without importing every bank statute or remedy 12. Continuous backing does not become a universal real-time monitoring/API requirement 13. Parent/shared frameworks are allowed, but subsidiary management must meaningfully participate 14. Internal audit need not take one organizational form 15. Interest rates affect assets, earnings and demand through different channels 16. There is no universal growth-rate cap, but the operation must support its growth 17. Insider/affiliate risk is tested transaction by transaction and in the aggregate 18. The service-provider duty includes contracts and evidence of performance 19. Stress tests must connect portfolio value and cash access 20. Required FX hedges do not become eligible reserve assets 21. Smart contracts and advanced AI appear in the comments without a technology-specific approval regime 22. Board responsibility survives removal of a required officer title 23. No privacy technology is a blanket compliance credential 24. Key and ledger controls must be maintained as assets and threats change 25. Incident notice depends on misuse risk; a criminal-investigation delay applies specifically to customer notice 26. Operational resilience includes the outside systems and a new ledger decision Additions to the initial overview Next wave

title: Economic savings depend on selected baselines, populations and financing assumptions
description: Complete saved reading and source links
search_context: Research Packages/Fintech and Private Rails/Retail Payment Terminal Transition 2026-07-28/genius-implementation-gap-2026-08-17/OCC Full Rule Reading 2026-10-21/WAVE 10 EFFECTIVE DATE ECONOMICS AND PAPERWORK.md Answer and coverage 1. January 18 follows the statutory backstop, not an invented publication date 2. Major-rule and OIRA review determinations are different from collection approval 3. Treasury-demand benefits depend on substitution and supply responses 4. Other short-debt benefits depend on imperfect substitution 5. The chosen counterfactual removes the Act and its implementing framework together 6. Several populations serve different calculations 7. Market forecasts and a company announcement are model inputs, not current permissions 8. Monetization and reserve-composition costs are often assumed already absorbed 9. The two-hour reserve-report estimate is not the whole monthly control system 10. Monthly reserve examination is not a monthly issuer-wide financial-statement audit 11. Low estimated redemption cost relies on competitive practices and the legal endpoint 12. The economic section retains a seven-day extension that the final rule does not grant 13. The capital-cost calculation assumes the floor and zero incremental issuer-assessed capital 14. The 0.48% expense proxy is not the legal backstop formula 15. Financing rates and debt mix are assumed prices, not instrument permissions 16. The headline capital savings can be reproduced from the displayed assumptions 17. Zero custody cost rests on existing specialist practices 18. The weekly and examination cost model uses only the incremental nonbank population 19.
